newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Five Tajik gunmen die after shoot-out with police.
newsitem.headline: Five Tajik gunmen die after shoot-out with police.

text.p: Five gunmen suspected of being involved in last week's assassination attempt on Tajikistan's leader were killed on Sunday in a shoot-out with police.
President Imomali Rakhmonov was injured last Wednesday when a hand grenade exploded near his car in the town of Khudjand in the north of the war-torn former Soviet republic.

Rakhmonov's spokesman Zafar Saidov told Reuters the gunmen had opened fire on the police after refusing to hand over their weapons. Three men were shot dead and a fourth, the head of the group Khorshyed Abdushukurov, killed himself, Saidov said.
A fifth gunman blew himself up with a hand-grenade, local television later reported.
Three police were badly injured in the clash, Saidov said.
The Tajik government has so far not blamed any one group for the assassination attempt on Rakhmonov, which it has branded a "terrorist act".
Two people were killed and scores injured in the attack. Rakhmonov was wounded in the legs and still has to undergo an operation to remove all the shrapnel.
On Saturday Saidov said about 10 people had been detained by the authorities in connection with the attack but gave no details on the arrests.
Tajikistan, a remote mountain state which borders Afghanistan and China, is still reeling from a four-year civil war which has claimed the lives of tens of thousands. Armed bands roam the country.

Both Tajikistan's armed Islamic opposition, Rakhmonov's main foe in the civil war, and the National Revival of Tajikistan bloc, part of the republic's so-called third political force and based around Khudjand, have denied any involvement in the attack on the president.
Diplomats and opposition sources say the attack could be a reaction to the government's recent crushing of a prison riot in Khudjand, in which 20 people died.
